text: The moon climbed high above the sleeping gums.
Sunny wandered where the shadows softly fell.
A rustle came from up among the leaves,
a gentle scrabble on a mossy branch.
A little ringtail possum, grey and soft,
with big round eyes and a curling, twirling tail.
Its tail wrapped round the branches like a spring,
holding tight as it climbed from tree to tree.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a lovely climb.”
“The treetops are my home,” it softly said.
It nibbled on a leaf, then curled its tail
and looked at Sunny with its shining eyes.
“Up here it's cosy, safe, and warm,” it said,
“tucked among the leaves beneath the stars.”
They watched the moon slide slowly through the leaves,
silver light on every quiet branch.
The possum yawned and curled into a ball,
its twirly tail wrapped gently round its nose.
It nestled in a hollow, soft with bark,
and closed its big round eyes against the night.
Sunny found a bed of leaves below
and snuggled down beneath the whispering tree.
The night was calm. The gum leaves gently swayed.
Everything was peaceful, warm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy as the branches swayed.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the sleeping possum,
both of them dreaming in the gentle dark.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little possum.
Goodnight, sleepy trees. Goodnight, little one.
